scenes.title: 1947 Winnenden Clinic Desk: Crisp Fine-Print Reading Yet a Blank Tabletop Mirror Until a Loved One Speaks

layout.description: Sunlit 1947 European neurology consultation desk holding a fine-print reading card, a brass-trimmed wooden tabletop mirror, three framed black-and-white family portrait photographs, and an open doorway where a visiting relative steps in silently before speaking.

positions.who: Patient S. (2.5D matte cream-white vinyl adult in neat 1947 wool cardigan and collared shirt)
positions.where: seated at the oak consultation desk reading the tiny eye-chart line cleanly, staring puzzled into the tabletop mirror, then rising in instant recognition the millisecond the visitor speaks

positions.who: Joachim Bodamer (2.5D matte cream-white vinyl neurologist in crisp 1947 white physician coat and tie)
positions.where: standing across the desk exchanging the fine-print reading card for the tabletop mirror and family portraits

positions.who: Visiting family member (2.5D matte cream-white vinyl older woman in 1947 tailored coat)
positions.where: pausing silently in the sunlit doorway (unrecognized) before speaking one warm greeting

props.name: brass-trimmed wooden tabletop mirror and framed family portraits
props.period_detail: stages Bodamer's 1947 discovery of 0% silent face recognition alongside intact feature vision
props.physical_behavior: State-A tilted toward Patient S. as he tilts head in blank confusion -> State-B set down briskly on desk as he turns toward the speaking voice at the door

props.name: fine-print clinical reading card and pocket watch object tray
props.period_detail: proves 20/20 visual acuity and intact everyday object naming right beside complete face blindness
props.physical_behavior: State-A held up at reading distance and read aloud effortlessly -> State-B placed beside portraits contrasting sharp vision with zero face ID

actions.verb_sequence: reads tiny print card aloud cleanly -> peers into tabletop mirror shaking head blankly -> hears visitor speak one word at doorway -> stands up immediately with open-armed warmth
places mirror beside fine-print card -> records 0% silent face ID vs 100% voice recognition in his 1947 clinical ledger

reactions.reaction: puzzled brow in front of silent mirror melting into instant warm recognition upon hearing the voice

scenes.wardrobe: 1947 European clinic dress: crisp white physician coat over dark tie; wool knit cardigan and pleated trousers; tailored wool overcoat.
scenes.lighting: Bright high-key European tall-window daylight across warm oak desk and brass mirror.
scenes.recognition_hook: He can read the smallest print on the desk — yet stares straight into a mirror at himself and straight at his own mother until she speaks a single word!

key_visual.description: a sunlit 1947 neurology clinic desk with a fine-print reading card, family portraits, and a wooden tabletop mirror where a seated adult stares blankly until turning warmly toward a speaking visitor

scenes.title: 1985 Iowa Sweat-Sensor Lab: Palm Conductance Recognizes Loved Ones When Conscious Speech Says 'Stranger'
scenes.era: 1985, University of Iowa Hospitals neurology lab (Tranel & Damasio)

layout.description: Clean sunlit clinical table where a 52-year-old prosopagnosic adult wired with gentle palm skin-conductance clips views shuffled family and stranger photographs beside an ink polygraph chart.

positions.where: volunteer shaking head 'Never met him' at a spouse photograph while the polygraph pen leaps sharply upward

props.name: shuffled family-vs-stranger portrait deck and electrodermal pen graph
props.period_detail: captures Tranel & Damasio's (1985 Science) covert recognition spike
props.physical_behavior: State-A flat ink line on stranger photo -> State-B tall sharp ink spike the instant a spouse photo lands on the desk

actions.verb_sequence: lays stranger photo down (flat needle) -> lays spouse photo down (volunteer shakes head NO while sweat needle jumps high)

reactions.reaction: points to the covert autonomic spike proving emotional familiarity survived without conscious face ID

scenes.wardrobe: 1985 academic blazer, collared shirt, and white clinical coat.
scenes.recognition_hook: Her mouth honestly says 'I have never seen this man in my life' — while her palm sweat sensor leaps in instant recognition of her husband!

scenes.title: Sunlit Outdoor Saturday Farmers' Market: The 1-in-50 Out-of-Context Encounter Rescued by Five Kind Words
scenes.era: Modern sunlit outdoor weekend neighborhood farmers' market walkway

layout.description: Open-air sunlit Saturday farmers' market sidewalk lined with produce crates where a 46-year-old adult hesitates when an office colleague walks up wearing casual weekend sunhat and polo — then lights up instantly the second the colleague greets them by name.

positions.who: 46-year-old developmental face-blind adult (holding woven market basket)
positions.where: pausing uncertainly on the sunlit brick market walkway when a coworker out of office attire waves silently

positions.who: Friendly office colleague (in weekend sunhat and linen shirt)
positions.where: stepping up with a warm wave and speaking their name aloud ('Hey Sam, it's Maya from third floor!')
positions.facing: facing colleague on sunlit market walkway

props.name: weekend sunhat and woven farmers' market produce basket
props.period_detail: shows how changing hairstyle/hat outside office context trips ~2% of adults with developmental face blindness
props.physical_behavior: State-A silent wave across market stall (hesitant pause) -> State-B spoken name greeting triggering an immediate warm handshake

actions.verb_sequence: waves silently in weekend sunhat (colleague squints uncertainly) -> speaks warm name greeting aloud -> both clasp hands laughing

reactions.reaction: instant relieved smile as voice bypasses the fusiform bottleneck

scenes.wardrobe: Relaxed weekend outdoor wear: woven sunhat, sky-blue linen shirt, cotton cardigan, market tote.
scenes.lighting: Warm golden morning sunlight across open-air market canopies and brick sidewalk.
scenes.recognition_hook: One in fifty adults walks past friends at the weekend market when haircuts or hats change — until five spoken words unlock instant recognition!
